subject: Request: early off-ramp credit + rewrite of ramp/opt-out language
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novamed.health>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Novamed <procurement@novamed.health>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: early off-ramp credit + ramp rewrite

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the draft SOW. We appreciate the flexibility so far. Two items surfaced in our legal/procurement review that are deal blockers for us to sign this week:

1) Early termination / off-ramp: We need a soft-credit if we choose to wind down the pilot before the commit period ends. Ideally a pro-rated credit to cover onboarding and tooling costs (we suggested a 30% credit of remaining committed spend if termination happens within the first 90 days).

2) Ramp schedule / opt-out language: The current ramp schedule ties us to staged capacity increases and a fairly strict opt-out process that requires a 60-day notice and an approval sash through the vendor. We need the opt-out process simplified and a defined grace window during which we can scale back without financial penalty.

I've attached our suggested SOW redlines and a short table with proposed ramp milestones. Can Redwood confirm whether these two items are possible on enterprise terms, or whether we need to escalate for an exception?

We are on a tight timeline to close this month. Appreciate quick visibility.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Technology Partnerships
Novamed Health

Attachments: Novamed-SOW-draft-v3.pdf, redwood_ramp_table.xlsx

Daniel —

Thanks for the clear redlines and the ramp table. I can discuss options, but the specific ask (30% credit within first 90 days + removing the 60-day approval gate) is outside standard PLG/Committed terms and will require a deal desk + exec OK.

Quick summary of what I can offer without escalation:
- Move to 45-day notice for a single-step scale-down (instead of 60) — requires updated billing cadence but no credit.
- Add a 30-day grace period during ramp milestone transitions where we won't enforce immediate capacity enforcement (operational only).

What I need to escalate to Deal Desk / Revenue Ops:
- The 30% pro-rated credit on remaining committed spend (non-standard; affects recognition and capacity planning).
- Language changes to allow Novamed unilateral opt-out inside the first 90 days without vendor approval.

Looping in Marissa (Head, Deal Desk) and Karthik (Sales Lead) for a fast decision — copying Vivek for any executive sign-off considerations. Attaching redlines to this thread.

Rachel

To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: ESCALATION: Novamed request for 30% early termination credit + opt-out rewrite (deal RDW-2026-1639)

Team —

Novamed (healthcare customer) is asking for two non-standard concessions: a 30% pro-rated credit on remaining committed spend if they terminate inside the first 90 days, and removal of the vendor-approval requirement for opt-out during that window. They say closing this month is critical.

Why this matters: the credit is material to revenue recognition and sets a precedent for other enterprise healthcare pilots. The opt-out rewrite removes a control that we use to manage capacity and forecast.

Options I see:
- Conservative (preferred): Offer a tiered early-exit credit: 60% of remaining committed spend in days 0–30, 40% in days 31–60, 25% in days 61–90 — with a cap and requirement that credits are applied as service credits (not cash) and require offboarding checklist completion. Maintain vendor approval for opt-out but automate the approval SLA to 5 business days.
- Middle ground (sales-favorable): Flat 30% credit within 90 days, but maintain vendor approval and require a minimum 30-day notice during opt-out window.
- Aggressive (riskier): Accept Novamed language as-is to close quickly — finance/legal will push back.

Attachments: redlined-terms-for-credits.docx, redwood_ramp_table.xlsx

Request: Can Marissa + Karthik weigh in with Deal Desk position? Vivek — if we need an exec concession, we will need sign-off on a one-off credit structure and carve-outs for healthcare vertical.

Thanks — I can be available now for a quick huddle.

Rachel

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ESCALATION: Novamed request for 30% early termination credit + opt-out rewrite (deal RDW-2026-1639)

FWIW — I ran high-level modeling with Finance. We cannot accept a flat 30% credit across 90 days; that will create P&L distortions and a precedent we cannot scale. Finance is comfortable with a tiered service-credit structure that phases down over the 90-day window. Key guardrails: credits must be applied as future service credit (no cash refunds), a maximum credit cap equal to 50% of remaining committed spend, and customer must complete the offboarding checklist within 30 days to unlock credit.

On the opt-out language: we should not remove the vendor-approval clause completely. We can amend to require an automated approval workflow (5 business days) and include an explicit grace window of 21 days where a single-step scale back is allowed without penalty. That preserves our operational controls while addressing their ask.

If Rachel can present the tiered structure to Novamed, I can sign off from Deal Desk. If Novamed insists on cash refunds or removing approval entirely, we should escalate to Vivek for exec waiver.

Marissa
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference

Attachment: internal-credit-models.xlsx (internal)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novamed.health>, Procurement Novamed <procurement@novamed.health>, Jill Turner <jill.turner@novamed.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: early off-ramp credit + ramp rewrite — proposed one-off structure

Daniel / team —

Appreciate the patience while we reviewed this. Per Deal Desk review, Redwood can offer a one-off, tiered early-exit service credit and a simplified opt-out SLA. Summary of the proposed concession (for signature):

- Early-exit service credit (applies to remaining committed spend if pilot is terminated): 60% credit for termination days 0–30; 40% for days 31–60; 25% for days 61–90. Credits are applied as Redwood service credits (no cash refunds) and may be used against future Redwood invoices for up to 12 months. Maximum total credit cannot exceed 50% of remaining committed spend.
- Opt-out / ramp language: Add a 21-day grace window during ramp transitions where Novamed may reduce capacity by one tier without penalty. Outside that window, maintain a 30-day notice for scale-backs. Vendor approval for opt-out will remain but is formalized into an automated workflow with a 5 business day SLA.
- Conditions: Novamed must complete the attached offboarding checklist within 30 days of notice to be eligible for credits. Credits will not apply if termination is for breach of contract.

If this is acceptable, we'll incorporate the redlines into the final SOW and route for signature (DocuSign link to follow). If you need any of the concessions adjusted (e.g., want a longer credit period or cash refund), we'll need an executive waiver.

Next steps: Please confirm by EOD 2026-08-17 so we can lock the SOW into the August close.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
